title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 in New Delhi
subtitle:
Nar Seva is Narayana Seva;Service to Society is Nation-Building at the Grassroots: Vice-President

Viksit Bharat Must Be Built on Compassion, Character and Social Responsibility: Vice-President

Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, Nasha Mukt Bharat Roadmap Important Initiatives for Drug-Free India: Vice-President

Vice-President Calls for Strengthening Spirit of Seva Bhav and Kartavya Bodh Among Youth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 as the Chief Guest in New Delhi and presented the Sant Eshwar Seva Samman to individuals and organisations recognised for their exemplary and selfless service to society.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Sant Eshwar Samman is a recognition of the spirit of selfless service and a celebration of India’s culture of compassion and responsibility. He extended his greetings and congratulations to all the awardees for their extraordinary contributions to the nation.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the Sant Eshwar Foundation and Rashtriya Sewa Bharati for instituting the awards and sustaining the initiative for 11 consecutive years. He said that by recognising countless individuals who work silently to strengthen society and make the nation more inclusive, the awards motivate others to follow the path of Seva.
Highlighting the timeless Indian tradition of service, the Vice-President said, “Our civilisational ethos has always taught us, ‘Nar Seva is Narayana Seva’.” He noted that the great saints and thinkers of Bharat have inspired people to rise above narrow boundaries of self and dedicate themselves to the welfare of others.
Referring to the goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Vice-President emphasised that development cannot be measured only through economic growth, infrastructure or technological advancement. A truly developed India, he said, is one where every citizen experiences dignity, opportunity and hope.
He said that every citizen is a stakeholder in the nation’s progress and that the work of service organisations and individuals constitutes nation-building at the grassroots. Citing the Swachh Bharat Mission as an example, he said the initiative demonstrated how Jan Bhagidari can transform a government programme into a people’s movement.
The Vice-President also highlighted the serious threat posed by narcotic drugs and substance abuse to the health and future of the youth. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan in August this year, while Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat 2029 Roadmap. He said that both initiatives are important steps towards building a drug-free India.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for development to be accompanied by compassion, character and social responsibility, and congratulated all the awardees. He expressed the hope that their lives would inspire more citizens, particularly the youth, to dedicate themselves to the welfare of society and strengthen the spirit of Seva Bhav and Kartavya Bodh.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Interacts with Captain Smit Machchhar
subtitle:
PM Commends His Courage and Presence of Mind in Saving Passengers' Lives

Today the entire country can proudly say that we Indians are not people who take lives, we are people who save lives: PM

Today is Gandhi Jayanti; what the true essence of non-violence is, you have demonstrated by living it: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today interacted with Captain Smit Machchhar through a video call. He began the conversation by inquiring about his health, assuring him that the entire country is praying for his recovery. He commended the pilot’s courage, patience, and swift presence of mind in taking critical decisions in a fraction of a second to save numerous lives. He pointed out that despite battling life and death and sustaining severe injuries, the Captain prioritized the safety of his passengers over his own life, enhancing the honor of 140 crore countrymen. “Today the entire country can proudly say that we Indians are not people who take lives, we are people who save lives,” emphasized Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister fondly recalled his conversation with the pilot’s family members, including Bhupendra bhai, Geeta bahen, and Sonal bahen. He praised Geeta bahen for instilling profound cultural values into her son, observing that she had completely absorbed and lived the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita.
The Prime Minister listened carefully as Captain Smit, calling him his biggest ideal, recounted how seventeen years of flying experience helped him realize the aircraft was going down. He heard the pilot describe the harrowing moment of making a final push to open the door, determined not to let the passengers die despite being heavily trapped and wounded. He deeply appreciated the Captain drawing spiritual strength from reciting the Hanuman Chalisa during his struggle for survival. He acknowledged that the Captain becoming emotional after enduring such a struggle is an entirely natural response. "Your brave actions have made the entire world eager to speak with you, and your family has truly brought glory to the nation," affirmed Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister highlighted the widespread emotional solidarity across the nation, noting that special prayers and aartis are being conducted from Savarkundla to Wadhwan for the pilot’s longevity. He lauded the Captain’s resolve to view his recovery as a patient journey, and appreciated hearing how the pilot recites the Hanuman Chalisa daily with his two-year-old son to stay connected to Indian culture. He extended heartfelt gratitude to the governments of Saudi Arabia and the UAE for providing outstanding medical care, echoing the Captain's sentiment about the immense love received from the local people. He noted that the Captain's actions protected the dignity and standing of all Indian pilots globally. “Today is Gandhi Jayanti; what the true essence of non-violence is, you have demonstrated by living it,” observed Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister conversed affectionately in Gujarati, inquiring after the Captain's young children, Bobby and Jiwa. He expressed profound admiration for the pilot's parents and his wife, Sonalbahen, who maintained remarkable poise and faith without a single trace of complaint during recent conversations. He assured the Captain that he remains just a phone call away and promised to listen to the inside details of the incident once they meet in person. He wished him a complete and speedy recovery while emphasizing that the entire country stands firmly with him. “Get well very soon so we can meet; God bless you and Jai Hind,” asserted Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of Prime Minister’s conversation with Captain Smit Machchhar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister –
Smit, Namaste.
Captain Smit –
Jai Hind, Sir. Namaste, Sir.
Prime Minister –
How are you now, how is your health?
Captain Smit –
Sir, everything is fine, Sir, all fine.
Prime Minister –
See, the entire nation is praying for you. The chanting of
Mahamrityunjaya
is happening everywhere.
Captain Smit –
Yes, Sir.
Prime Minister –
Your courage, your patience, and your presence of mind - in a fraction of a second you took so many decisions…
Captain Smit –
Yes, Sir.
Prime Minister –
And saved so many lives. Today the entire nation can proudly say that we Indians are not people who take lives, we are people who save lives.
Captain Smit –
Absolutely, Sir.
Prime Minister –
And even when you had such a big wound on your body, when you yourself were fighting the battle between life and death, at that time you did not care for your own life, but cared for the lives of all the passengers. And most importantly, you raised the honor of 1.4 billion countrymen.
Captain Smit –
Thank you, Sir.
Prime Minister –
And that is why I feel pride from the depths of my heart.
Captain Smit –
Sir, I… sorry.
Prime Minister –
Yesterday I had the opportunity to speak with Bhupendra Bhai, with Geeta Behen, with Sonal Behen. I could not speak with Java and Bobby. But I told Geeta Behen that though her name is Geeta, she has truly absorbed the essence of Krishna’s Gita. And she has shaped Smit’s life with those very values of the Gita.
Captain Smit –
Absolutely, Sir.
Prime Minister –
Smit, now I would like to hear from you.
Captain Smit –
Sir, for me… I was telling Sir also… you are my greatest, greatest ideal, Sir. And you are calling me like this, encouraging me. I feel very, very, very proud. At that moment, Sir, yes, I was fighting for my life. But there was a moment when I realized that if I did not do something… because I had fallen, I had so many injuries, I was trapped below. And at that time I said to myself, if I do not get up… Sir, I have been flying aircraft in FZ for 17 years. I have been a captain for the past 11 years. And I know, even with my eyes closed, what is happening in the aircraft. When I was lying down, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. And I knew clearly that this was the last push - if Smit could just do it - the door was right there. Even then I was being hit, but I opened it, Sir. Then everyone came out, and everyone else had their role too. But knowingly I was saying, I was acting for my own life, but at the same time I knew I could not let them all die. After that, people here, in Saudi, here too - I could not have received better care or medical attention. And Sir, I am just… I am only in positivity. Whenever I feel pain, only one thing comes to me - I recite the
Hanuman Chalisa.
At that time too, I was only reciting the
Hanuman Chalisa.
And I know it was God who saved me. And now, Sir, your call has come - I feel immense pride. Until now I did not feel it. Now I do, Sir. Sorry, I am crying in front of you, Sir.
Prime Minister –
Smit, if you cannot be emotional in front of me, then where else will you be?
Captain Smit –
Sir, I never thought that I would speak with you, never thought.
Prime Minister –
You have done such a great deed, brother, that every countryman today - even people around the world - are eager to see you, to speak with you. And this thing you told me about the
Hanuman Chalisa
- for that I bow to Geeta Behen, that she gave you such values, I bow to Bhupendra Bhai. And let me tell you, Smit, yesterday when I spoke with Sonal Behen, I was surprised - she spoke with such composure.
Captain Smit –
Yes, Sir.
Prime Minister –
She was speaking with such courage. Truly, I had never imagined that Sonal Behen would be able to speak with such composure in such circumstances. So I believe that, as a family, you have truly brought glory to the entire nation.
Captain Smit –
Sir, every morning when I pray, my two‑year‑old son sits in my lap and I recite the
Hanuman Chalisa
to him. I tell him what I have been taught, because today we may be living away from our country, but we should never be away from our culture.
Prime Minister –
That is absolutely right.
Captain Smit –
And now, here, it does not even feel as if we are away from the country. The people here are taking care of us with so much love and attention.
Prime Minister –
You may not know this, but in Savarkundla, in Wadhwan, people have created such an emotional atmosphere. And this is true across the whole of India. Yesterday, prayers, worship, and aarti were held in temples everywhere. Aarti was performed at pilgrimage sites across the country. Everyone is praying for your long life and good health. Therefore, you are certainly going to recover soon. India is eagerly waiting to welcome you. Now, whatever physical pain you may be experiencing, I can understand. You are a brave man, so perhaps you have made it easier for yourself to bear your wounds.
Captain Smit –

I am looking at it as a journey, something that will happen slowly, step by step, and will take time. But I am very, very confident that I will recover and become completely healthy again.
Prime Minister –
I also express my heartfelt gratitude to the Saudi government and the UAE government for taking such good care of you. I am grateful to them as well. Smit, whenever you feel the need, I am only a phone call away.
Captain Smit –
Thank you, Sir.
Prime Minister –
But let me tell you, what you have done is truly extraordinary. Yesterday I was looking at the emotions people expressed on social media. People said that if this had not happened the way it did, nobody knows what India would have gone through, what all the pilots of India would have gone through, how all Indian pilots would have been viewed. You saved all of that. You have done something truly remarkable.
Captain Smit –
Yes, Sir.
Prime Minister –
When we meet, I will hear all the inside details later, because I do not want to discuss such things with you over a mobile phone.
Captain Smit –
Alright, Sir.
Prime Minister –
And you focus on recovering completely. The entire nation is with you.
Captain Smit –
Thank you, Sir.
Prime Minister –
I do not want to tire you out any further. My very best wishes are with you. Today is Gandhi Jayanti. You have shown through your actions what non‑violence truly means.

Prime Minister –
Alright then, Jai Shri Krishna. Jai Shri Krishna, my son. Let us also speak a little Gujarati.

Prime Minister –

I spoke yesterday with Bhupendra Bhai and Geeta Behen at Mumbai Airport. Even then, there was not a trace of complaint. They simply said that God would do what is best.

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN THE PROGRAMME ‘KNOW YOUR LEADERS’

LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON YOUTH TO DRAW INSPIRATION FROM THE LIVES AND IDEALS OF MAHATMA GANDHI AND SHRI LAL BAHADUR SHASTRI

YOUTH MUST EMBRACE TRUTH, NON-VIOLENCE, SIMPLICITY, DISCIPLINE, AND A STRONG SENSE OF DUTY TO BUILD A VIKSIT BHARAT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

MORE THAN 500 YOUNG PARTICIPANTS FROM ACROSS INDIA PAY HOMAGE TO MAHATMA GANDHI AND SHRI LAL BAHADUR SHASTRI IN THE CENTRAL HALL OF SAMVIDHAN SADAN
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla; Union Minister of Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh; Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda; Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju; Leader of the Opposition in Rajya Sabha Shri Mallikarjun Kharge; Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Shri Rahul Gandhi; Shri Nitin Nabin, MP; Members of Parliament, former Members, and other dignitaries paid floral tributes at the portraits of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, on the occasion of their birth anniversaries, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan today.
Secretary-General of Lok Sabha Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and Secretary-General of Rajya Sabha Shri P.C. Mody also paid floral tributes on the occasion.
On this occasion, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla, addressing students from different parts of the country in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan as part of the ‘Know Your Leader’ Programme, called upon the youth to draw inspiration from the lives, ideals, and public service of Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, and to contribute with determination, discipline, and a strong sense of responsibility toward building a developed India.
Welcoming the young participants, the Speaker said that their presence in the historic Central Hall was an opportunity to connect with India's democratic and constitutional heritage. Mentioning Mahatma Gandhi, he noted that his life demonstrated the power of truth, morality, non-violence, and Satyagraha. At a time when much of the world was under colonial rule, Mahatma Gandhi showed that a movement based on truth and non-violence could give direction to the struggle for freedom. His ideas and philosophy subsequently inspired movements for freedom and justice across the world. Invoking the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, he urged the youth to study his life and ideas, saying that the more one understands his life and philosophy, the more one gains insight, courage, and a new perspective to face adversity and challenges. He said that Mahatma Gandhi's life teaches that even through simple means, lasting change can be brought about in the lives and minds of people. Self-reflection, discipline, perseverance, and firmness of purpose were integral to his life and remain relevant for the youth today.
Referring to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, Shri Birla highlighted his simplicity, honesty, high ideals, sense of duty, and firmness in decision-making. He recalled Shastriji’s inspiring call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan”, which gave direction to the nation during a challenging period and underlined the importance of national and food security. he said that although today's youth have access to technology, knowledge, and enormous resources, these alone cannot ensure the achievement of one's goals. Patience, ethical conduct, discipline, determination, and continuity of effort are equally essential. He called upon the youth to remain steadfast in their goals and not allow disappointment, fatigue, or setbacks to weaken their resolve. He stated that social responsibility must remain at the heart of the youth's journey and that their aim should be not merely personal achievement, but also contributing to the development and progress of the country. He urged them to use their knowledge, energy, and capabilities to help build and lead a new and developed India.
Concluding his address, Shri Birla called upon the participants to carry the message and inspiration of the programme to their schools, communities, and wherever they go. He said that they should leave the historic Constituent Assembly Hall with new inspiration, energy, and confidence, and with a renewed commitment to fulfill their duties and contribute to nation-building.
More than 500 school students from different parts of the country participated in the programme and witnessed the floral tributes paid to Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri in the historic Constituent Assembly Hall. Thirty-six selected young participants also spoke on the lives, ideals, thoughts, and contributions of the two national leaders, sharing their understanding of how their lives continue to inspire generations in India and across the world.
Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha Speaker also visited Rajghat and Vijay Ghat to pay his respects at the samadhis of Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, respectively.

content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held bilateral talks with Mr. Silvio Erkens, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, Netherlands, in New Delhi on 28th September 2026.
The meeting focused on reviewing ongoing cooperation in agriculture sector, and strengthening agricultural cooperation by exploring new areas of cooperation. Both sides reiterated their resolve to enhance productivity through modern technology, innovation and knowledge exchange.
Both sides discussed progress on establishment of 25 Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in the agriculture and horticulture sectors. title: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal Calls for WTO-Compliant Approach to Correcting Global Trade Distortions at the Concluding Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, U.S.
subtitle: Shri Piyush Goyal Reaffirms India’s Commitment to Eliminating Forced Labour, Calls for Evidence-Based Trade Measures
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 12:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and spoke in sessions on structural excess capacity and production, updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, ending forced labour in global supply chains, and the closing session.
Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Shri Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people, and is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in global supply chains. He said India’s manufacturing capacity serves its domestic and global needs and that, in the sectors identified by the G20 Presidency, India does not have structural excess capacity.
Shri Goyal said India shares the concerns of many Members that trade-distorting support in some economies can lead to dumping and predatory pricing. He said such concerns are addressed through WTO-consistent measures, including anti-dumping and countervailing duties, based on evidence and subject to judicial review. He emphasised that industrial capacity in itself is not the issue, while distortions can arise where geographical concentration of production is driven by hidden subsidies and support. He said diversification of production and supply chains is a legitimate objective, but cannot be used as a pretext for measures outside WTO rules or for shifting the burden of adjustment onto developing countries, which must retain policy space to industrialise. He also said that sharing of statistics and data should take place within existing mechanisms.
On updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, Shri Goyal said that India’s trade with G20 members depends on a transparent, non-discriminatory and rules-based trading system. He said Most-Favoured-Nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system, ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest trader and the largest trader. He emphasised that consensus remains central to the WTO and that special and differential treatment must be preserved to enable developing countries to catch up with developed economies. He also called for restoration of the two-tier dispute settlement system.
Speaking on ending forced labour in global supply chains, Shri Goyal said India’s commitment to the elimination of forced labour is absolute and unconditional. He noted that Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits forced labour as a fundamental right, enforceable by the Supreme Court. He said India has ratified ILO Conventions 29 and 105 and, in July 2026, amended its Foreign Trade Policy to prohibit the import of goods produced using forced labour.
Shri Goyal said measures at the border must be based on specific and verifiable evidence rather than presumptions about entire countries, regions or sectors, and must respect due process and WTO rules. He said the International Labour Organization is the competent, universal and tripartite body for labour standards. India supports the objective of eliminating forced labour and voluntary exchange of good practices among G20 members, provided that such cooperation does not involve monitoring of members, create new obligations or result in information being used as a basis for unilateral trade action.
Shri Goyal thanked Ambassador Greer and the United States G20 Presidency for the arrangements and hospitality extended in Milwaukee. Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s words that issues that cannot be resolved together should not come in the way of those that can, Shri Goyal said India participated in the Meeting in that spirit and, across all four themes, shared its concerns and offered constructive inputs.
The Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to a rules-based, fair, equitable, non-discriminatory, transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core. He emphasised the importance of preserving policy space for developing countries to grow and feed their people, while upholding decision-making by consensus. Shri Goyal extended India’s full support to the United Kingdom for its G20 Presidency in 2027.
On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal held bilateral meetings with the Minister for Trade and Tourism of Australia, the Minister of Commerce of Saudi Arabia, the Minister Delegate for Foreign Trade and Economic Attractiveness of France, the Minister for Trade of the Republic of Korea and the Minister of International Trade of Canada.

title: APEDA Facilitates Export of Bihar’s Makhana from Purnea to Greece
subtitle: Export-led Market Access Enhances Farmer Realisation and Expands Bihar’s Makhana Exports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 11:55AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a consignment of 1 MT of Popped (Phool) Makhana from Purnea, Bihar, for export to Greece, marking another step towards expanding international market access for Bihar’s traditional Makhana and creating opportunities for improved farmer realisation through export-oriented value chains.
The consignment, sourced by Indo Global Export, Belouri, Purnea, is being exported to Greece through S. S Foods Exports Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi. The shipment will move from Mundra Port in India to Piraeus Port in Greece.
The export has also resulted in higher price realisation compared with the prevailing domestic market selling price, highlighting the potential of international markets to create additional value for Makhana producers. Such export-led market access can strengthen linkages between producers and international buyers while creating opportunities for improved returns to farmers.
India is the global leader in Makhana production, with Bihar contributing around 80-85% of the country’s production. Makhana cultivation in Bihar spans over 35,000 hectares across 10 districts. The sector is supported by technical interventions at the grassroots level from Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, and ICAR-National Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga.
The flag-off programme was chaired by Agriculture Minister, Government of Bihar, Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha, in the presence of Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, and Director, Horticulture, Agriculture Department, Government of Bihar, Shri Abhishek Kumar, along with senior officers of the Government of Bihar and other stakeholders associated with the Makhana export value chain.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha said, “The export marks an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continues to reach international markets. India exported more than 7000 MT of makhana and value-added makhana products valued at USD 22 million during FY 2025-26 across more than 20 international destinations.”
He further stated that the Government of Bihar is working towards an Agri Export Policy aimed at supporting farmers and improving their incomes through export promotion. He also highlighted that packhouses have been developed to support the Makhana export value chain. He commended APEDA for its continued efforts towards expanding Makhana exports and improving farmer realisation.
The export from Purnea to Greece is part of growing efforts to connect Bihar’s Makhana producers and exporters with international markets. With its strong traditional and cultural association with Bihar, Makhana has emerged as an important product in India’s agricultural export basket.
APEDA has been facilitating market linkages and supporting exporters in taking Indian Makhana to international markets. Makhana exports are also expanding into European markets, with growing opportunities for Indian producers and avenues for diversification beyond traditional destinations. These efforts are helping connect Makhana producers in Bihar with international demand while creating opportunities for improved farmer realisation and greater participation of producer groups in the export value chain.

title: Government Extends Operational Timelines of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) Intervention to Support Exporters Amid West Asia Logistics Disruptions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 11:01AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In view of the continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and its impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions, the Department of Commerce has vide Notification No.37/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF – Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM).
Component II of the RELIEF scheme encourages exporters to obtain ECGC cover for upcoming shipments to the specified regions, with 95% risk coverage. The component is available for Stand Alone Policies or Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after 16 March 2026. The types of cargo covered under the benefits include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL), and Reefer containers (excluding energy shipments). Further, this component of RELIEF ensures that the premium paid by exporters shall not be increased beyond the pre-disruption level for the eligible period.
RELIEF was launched on 19 March 2026 as a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters affected by extraordinary freight escalation, heightened insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and wider West Asia maritime corridor.
The above extension reflects Government of India’s commitment to ensure export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting exporters amid the prevailing geopolitical and logistics uncertainties.

title: "Context Matters, Care Matters, Compassion Matters": CEO BHASHINI at MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave
subtitle: Scientific Conclave on Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice held as part of MNS Centenary Year celebrations
date:
Posted On:
                02 OCT 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Military Nursing Service (MNS)
organised the
Scientific Conclave on “Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice: Harmonizing Technology with Compassionate Care”
as part of the closing ceremony of its
Centenary Year 2026
at Manekshaw Centre, Delhi Cantt. The conclave brought together senior leadership, nursing professionals, healthcare practitioners and technology stakeholders to deliberate on the evolving role of digital innovation in strengthening healthcare delivery and nursing practice.
Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, BHASHINI
, was invited as the
Keynote Speaker
at the inaugural ceremony of the Scientific Conclave, where he delivered a keynote address titled
“Wired in Wellness: The Scope of Opportunities of Digital Health in Transforming the Healthcare Landscape.”
General Dhiraj Seth, PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, Chief of the Army Staff, was the Chief Guest for the inaugural ceremony. The programme also witnessed the release of the MNS Diary and the Nursing Research Compendium, along with the e-release of the scientific souvenir titled “Digital Pulse of Nursing: Connecting Technology, Transforming Care.”
In his keynote address, Shri Nag highlighted the transformative potential of digital technologies in healthcare, emphasising that language, context and healthcare-specific data are essential to building technology that is accessible, accurate and responsive to the needs of patients and healthcare professionals.
He outlined the four pillars of BHASHINI and its growing role in healthcare, including speech, translation and other language technologies, which can reduce communication barriers and make healthcare systems more inclusive across India's diverse linguistic landscape.
He stressed the need for medical and nursing glossaries as foundational language resources for healthcare-focused AI systems. While medical terminology requires consistency, patients often describe symptoms in everyday language, and the same condition may be expressed differently across languages, regions and contexts. AI systems therefore need healthcare-specific language data to understand this diversity accurately. A well-developed glossary can connect clinical terminology with everyday language, creating a common language layer between healthcare professionals, patients and AI systems.
Shri Nag also underlined the importance of language in care delivery. Since healthcare communication spans diverse linguistic and social contexts, language, datasets, digital literacy and clinical accuracy are key to the effective adoption of digital health technologies.
He spoke about the BHASHINI Domain Innovation Challenge in Healthcare, which encourages technology-led solutions to practical challenges in healthcare communication. Among the solutions highlighted was an AI-powered voice-to-text tool for OPD prescriptions, demonstrating how speech and language technologies can support clinical workflows and enable more efficient documentation. He noted the potential of voice-first and multilingual technologies to bridge the gap between technology and the realities of healthcare delivery, particularly where communication must move seamlessly between clinical terminology and the language patients use.
Speaking on language in compassionate healthcare, Shri Nag said, "Context matters, care matters, compassion matters, and healthcare, all three become even more important when we are communicating with people in a language they understand."
The discussions at the Scientific Conclave reflected the growing intersection of nursing, healthcare, digital technologies and AI, while underscoring the need to keep technological advancement grounded in the human dimensions of care.
The participation of CEO, BHASHINI, at the MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave highlighted the importance of building digital health solutions that recognise India's linguistic diversity and support healthcare professionals and patients through technologies that are accessible, context-aware and designed around real-world communication needs.
The Scientific Conclave formed an important part of the closing celebrations of the Centenary Year of the Military Nursing Service, commemorating a century of dedicated service and recognising the evolving role of nursing in an increasingly technology-enabled healthcare ecosystem.
About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, enabling greater accessibility to digital services through Language AI.

title: Union Environment Minister and CM (West Bengal) release 1st Tigress in Buxa Tiger Reserve under Tiger Reintroduction Programme
subtitle: Focus on complementing Natural Recovery through Scientifically-guided Interventions and Community Participation
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 1:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant milestone for tiger conservation in India, a tigress was released in Buxa Tiger Reserve (W. Bengal) today, in the presence of the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav and Chief Minister (W. Bengal), Shri Suvendu Adhikari. It marks a fitting beginning of India's Wildlife Week 2026, with the initiation of a phased Tiger Reintroduction Programme aimed at restoring a viable and self-sustaining tiger population in this historically important tiger landscape.
In a social media post after the release, Shri Bhupender Yadav stated that inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s push for landscape conservation and species protection, today the significant promise to reintroduce tiger in Buxa has been fulfilled. He thanked Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary and West Bengal Chief Minister Shri Suvendu Adhikari for their support in this successful reintroduction.
Inspired by PM Shri @narendramodi ji’s push for landscape conservation and species protection, today we have fulfilled the significant promise to reintroduce tiger in Buxa. 

T138 has been brought from Valmiki Tiger Reserve from Bihar to Buxa. 

I thank Bihar Chief Minister Shri @samrat4bjp and West Bengal Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB for their support in this successful reintroduction.

#TigerBackInBuxa
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
October 2, 2026
Buxa has historically been an important tiger landscape of North Bengal. Declared a Tiger Reserve in 1983, it forms part of a larger ecological landscape with connectivity to forests and protected areas of Bhutan and Assam. Over the decades, however, habitat degradation and fragmentation, changes in land use and decline in prey availability affected the ecological conditions required to sustain a resident tiger population. The Reserve subsequently witnessed a prolonged absence of a stable resident tiger population.
The recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort. The Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has since 2018 been implemented collaboratively. The focus has been on rebuilding the ecological foundations necessary for tiger recovery through habitat improvement, prey-base augmentation, strengthening protection and monitoring, scientific assessment and capacity building. More than 800 chital have been released to supplement the prey base, while approximately 380 hectares of grassland have been restored or converted over the past eight years. Scientific monitoring has indicated a positive trend in prey abundance.
Long-term monitoring has also provided encouraging evidence of tiger movement through the landscape. Camera traps recorded tigers in 2021, 2023 and 2026. Notably, an individual photographed in 2023 was matched with a tiger from Manas Tiger Reserve in Assam, providing evidence of natural movement between adjoining tiger landscapes. The present augmentation programme seeks to complement natural recovery through carefully planned and scientifically guided interventions.
Today’s release of the tigress marks the first phase of a planned, phased and adaptive recovery programme. The feline was translocated from Valmiki Tiger Reserve (Bihar), which was undertaken following assessment of relevant ecological, veterinary and management parameters and in accordance with established protocols. The animal will be subject to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping and field-based monitoring, enabling assessment of its movement, adaptation, health and behaviour.
The programme is not merely about bringing tigers back to Buxa. Its objective is to create the conditions in which a tiger population can establish, breed and ultimately become viable and self-sustaining. Further augmentation, wherever scientifically justified, will be undertaken in a phased manner based on habitat and prey availability, protection preparedness, population viability, monitoring outcomes and expert advice.
Community participation remains central to this recovery effort. The programme has engaged 64 Eco-Development Committees/Joint Forest Management Committees, with emphasis on community dialogue, livelihood opportunities, human-wildlife conflict mitigation and conservation-linked benefits. As tiger recovery progresses, continued community engagement and effective mechanisms for coexistence will remain an integral part of the programme.
The recovery of tigers in Buxa is also significant at the landscape level. Its ecological linkages with North Bengal, Assam and Bhutan provide opportunities for movement and dispersal of wildlife across a larger connected landscape. Strengthening Buxa therefore has implications not only for tiger conservation but also for the conservation of forests, grasslands, prey species and wider biodiversity.
The release today represents the beginning of a new chapter in Buxa’s conservation journey. The measure of success will not be the number of tigers released, but the establishment, over time, of a healthy, free-ranging and self-sustaining tiger population supported by secure habitat, adequate prey, effective protection, ecological connectivity, scientific monitoring and meaningful participation of local communities.

Eleven persons have been apprehended in the three operations.
Seized Ivory Tusks and articles
In an operation targeting illegal trade in elephant ivory, DRI officers conducted a decoy operation based on specific intelligence regarding attempts to illicitly sell four elephant tusks, including intricately carved ivory articles. The operation resulted in the recovery of the four wildlife articles and apprehension of three persons involved in the transaction. Possession without licence and trade/dealing in elephant ivory and articles made therefrom are prohibited under Section 49B of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. The seized articles and the detained persons were subsequently handed over to the jurisdictional Forest Range Officer for further investigation and necessary action.

one leopard skin.

The investigations and follow up searches resulted in recovery of incriminating evidence relating to the alleged poaching, possession, transportation and proposed sale of tiger body parts. title: DRI busts two-way gold-diamond smuggling syndicate at Mumbai airport
subtitle:
Seizure of around 8.5 kg foreign-origin gold and more than 1,100 carats of diamonds worth over Rs. 13.5 crore; 8 arrested

date:

                02 OCT 2026 9:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has busted a sophisticated two-way smuggling syndicate operating through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, resulting in the seizure of 8.564 kg of 24-carat foreign-origin gold valued at approximately Rs. 12.64 crore and 1,168.97 carats of diamonds valued at approximately Rs. 1.09 crore. Eight persons, including an airport staff member, six transit passengers and an Indian outbound passenger, have been arrested.
Seized diamonds
On 30.09.26, acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted an airport staff member in the departure area while he was handing over diamonds to an Indian passenger travelling to Dubai for their illicit export from India. During his personal search, the airport staff was also found carrying three capsules containing foreign-origin gold dust in wax form, which had been handed over to him by a transit passenger.
During further interrogation, the airport staff disclosed the identity of the transit passenger who had handed over the gold to him. The said passenger was subsequently intercepted. The airport staff further revealed that five more transit passengers arriving on different flights from Dubai, Doha, Jeddah and Fujairah were also scheduled to deliver smuggled gold to him.
Seized 23 capsules of gold
DRI officers maintained discreet surveillance and intercepted all five passengers while they were handing over gold capsules to the airport staff in the transit area. The passengers were travelling onward to Singapore and Dhaka after delivering the smuggled gold. All eight persons have been arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
In all, 23 capsules containing 24-carat foreign-origin gold dust in wax form, weighing 8.564 kg gross and valued at approximately Rs.12.64 crore, were recovered and seized. In addition, 1,168.97 carats of diamonds, comprising 132.17 carats of natural diamonds and 1,036.80 carats of lab-grown diamonds, collectively valued at approximately Rs.1.09 crore, were recovered and seized. The operation once again highlighted the insider threat involving compromised airport staff in facilitating gold smuggling through airports.
The operation has uncovered a distinctive two-way modus operandi, wherein the same airport staff member was allegedly facilitating the movement of contraband in both directions—receiving smuggled foreign-origin gold from international transit passengers for clandestine removal into India, while simultaneously facilitating the illicit export of diamonds to Dubai through an outbound passenger.

content:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting deeply mourns the untimely demise of three members of the Information and Broadcasting fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram on October 1, 2026. The vehicle carrying the officials fell into a gorge while they were on official duty.
The deceased are Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau and Central Bureau of Communication, Imphal; Shri Nampibou Marinmai, IIS, Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl; and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, Central Bureau of Communication, Field Office, Aizawl.
The tragic loss of three colleagues has deeply saddened the Ministry. Their untimely demise is a profound loss to their respective organisations and to the larger family of officials and professionals engaged in public communication and information dissemination across the country.
Dr. Engam Pame, 58, joined the Indian Information Service in 1994 after completing his MA in International Relations from the School of Social Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. During his more than three decades of service, he served in various capacities in Delhi, Imphal, Pune and Shillong, contributing to government communication, media coordination and public outreach.
As Additional Director General, PIB Imphal, Dr. Pame played an important role in strengthening communication and coordination with media organisations and government departments across the Northeast. One of the longest-serving Information Service Group A officers from the Northeast, he brought extensive field experience and a deep understanding of the region’s diverse communication landscape to his assignments. Dr. Pame belonged to the Zeme Naga community of Tamenglong district, Manipur. He is survived by his wife, Ajuna Pame, and a son and daughter.
Shri Nampibou Marinmai was an Indian Information Service officer and was serving as Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl. He was also Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC). He had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, where he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication.
Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, Shri Nampi made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. His experience in defence public relations and broadcasting enabled him to facilitate communication between institutions and the media. His professional commitment, dedicated service and cordial association with colleagues and media professionals will be remembered with respect. He is survived by his wife, son and daughter.
Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, CBC Field Office Aizawl, had joined government service in 1998. He was 52 and is survived by his wife, daughter and grandson.
Shri Gojendra Dey, Driver, CBC, Field Office, Aizawl, also sustained injuries in the accident and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. He is conscious and under medical care.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting stands with the bereaved families, colleagues and friends of the three officials in this hour of profound grief. Their years of dedicated service to the Government and their contribution to public communication will be remembered with respect and gratitude.

PMEGP, a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) plays a crucial role in promoting self-employment by enabling the establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Under the scheme, prospective entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of Margin Money (MM) subsidy on bank-sanctioned loans providing much needed impetus to enterprise creation.
Since FY 2014-15, around 8.12 lakh micro entrepreneurs have been assisted with MM Subsidy to the tune of Rs. 24,398.61 crore under PMEGP for generation of sustainable employment opportunities to ~73.08 lakh persons.
Turning Aspirations into Enterprises: PMEGP Driving Grassroots Transformation
PMEGP is transforming the aspirations of ordinary individuals into successful enterprises by providing easy access to credit supported by MM subsidy. It enables first-generation entrepreneurs to establish viable businesses, turning job seekers into job creators.
The success of PMEGP is best reflected in the inspiring journeys of its beneficiaries, who have transformed their entrepreneurial aspirations into thriving enterprises:
Skinkaanti Ayurveda – From Micro Enterprise to National Leader:
Founded by Smt. Pooja Sharma based in Parwanoo, Himachal Pradesh, Skinkaanti Ayurveda exemplifies remarkable growth from a modest micro-enterprise into India’s largest handmade soap manufacturing unit. Established with a project cost of Rs. 25 lakh and supported by State Bank of India,
the enterprise today records an impressive annual turnover of Rs. 30 crore and provides employment to 300 individuals, of which 95% are women
. By blending Ayurvedic principles with modern scientific techniques, the unit has achieved significant technological breakthroughs, including improved manufacturing efficiency and cost reduction, while supplying products across India through diverse retail and institutional channels.
M/s Ess Pee Quality Products – From PMEGP Support to Global Recognition:
Established by Shri Surender Pal Singh Nagi in Mohali, Punjab, M/s Ess Pee Quality Products has evolved into a globally competitive food processing enterprise. With an initial project cost of Rs. 21 lakh financed by Bank of Baroda,
the unit has grown into a Rs. 38 crore turnover business, generating employment for around 130 individuals
. The enterprise manufactures honey, cookies, and fruit jams, and exports to 26 countries, including the USA, Australia, and France. Its achievement of the prestigious AA+ BRCGS certification highlights its adherence to global quality and safety standards.
The success stories of the PMEGP entrepreneurs demonstrate the transformative impact of the scheme in fostering entrepreneurship, promoting scaling up of micro-enterprises and a key driver of employment generation and inclusive growth across the country.

transparent, sustainable and responsible development

title: 2.42 Lakh Special Gram Sabhas Across India Put Citizen-Centric Initiatives at the Heart of Grassroots Discussions on Gandhi Jayanti
subtitle: ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’ Gets Underway; Special Gram Sabhas Set the Stage for Panchayat Development Plans 2027-28
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country, with more than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on the GPDP Portal (https://gpdp.nic.in) and Panchayat NIRNAY Portal (https://meetingonline.gov.in). These Gram Sabhas witnessed enthusiastic and active participation of local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials. The Special Gram Sabhas also marked the commencement of the People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Panchayats will prepare their Panchayat Development Plans for the Financial Year 2027-28. In these 2.42 lakh special Gram Sabhas, schemes and pioneering initiatives of the Government of India, namely from the Ministry of Panchayati Raj; the Department of Rural Development; the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation; the Department of Consumer Affairs; the Department of Food and Public Distribution; the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; and the Department of Land Resources were placed at the center of the discussions.
The Special Gram Sabhas provided rural citizens with a direct platform to participate in discussions on key government initiatives and issues of local relevance. The wide-ranging deliberations covered enhanced devolution of Central Finance Commission grants to Panchayats, financial self-reliance through Own Source Revenue, secure property and land rights, assured employment and livelihoods, safe drinking water and sanitation, water security, food security, consumer protection and women’s economic empowerment, among other areas. Agenda and awareness material highlighting key government initiatives, including transformative governance reforms and citizen-centric measures undertaken over the last twelve years, were read out and deliberated upon. Local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials actively participated, sharing their experiences, perspectives and suggestions, which will contribute to enriching the Gram Panchayat Development Plans. The nationwide conduct of these Special Gram Sabhas was supported by the coordinated efforts of partner Ministries and Departments, along with their field and grassroots-level functionaries and MY Bharat volunteers. Their engagement across State, District, Block and Gram Panchayat levels helped facilitate meaningful dialogue on citizen-centric schemes and initiatives, while strengthening
Jan Bhagidari
and
Samvaad
at the grassroots. Adopting a Whole-of-Government approach, Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, along with senior officers of the Ministry and participating Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, remained in continuous touch with officials of States and Union Territories throughout the day, reviewing the progress of Special Gram Sabhas across the country and facilitating close coordination in the spirit of cooperative federalism. The coordinated efforts of States and Union Territories, supported by their Panchayati Raj Departments, district administrations and field functionaries, ensured the seamless conduct of this nationwide exercise on an unprecedented scale.
People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27 ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’
The People’s Plan Campaign, led by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in collaboration with 21 Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, reflects the Whole-of-Government approach under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Ministry has been rolling out the People’s Plan Campaign in all States and Union Territories since 2018 to enable Panchayats to prepare evidence-based, holistic and participatory plans. Under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, the Ministry supports training and capacity building across nine themes of local development. More than 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats prepare participatory Gram Panchayat Development Plans and upload them on the eGramSwaraj portal, while the Panchayat Advancement Index helps each Gram Panchayat identify its achievements and gaps. On this basis, the Gram Sabha can take a Sankalp on priority areas, advancing the Localisation of Sustainable Development Goals and the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Key reforms and achievements presented in the Special Gram Sabhas
Empowered and self-reliant Panchayats (Ministry of Panchayati Raj).
The Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended ₹4,35,236 crore for Rural Local Bodies for 2026-31, an increase of nearly 84 per cent over the Fifteenth Finance Commission, with the annual per capita grant rising from about ₹400 to nearly ₹950. The SAMARTH Panchayat Portal has registered over 57 lakh taxpayers and 15 lakh properties, and the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award carries incentives of up to ₹1 crore. Panchayat accounts now follow the six-tier structure used by the Union and State Governments, and more than 2.5 lakh Panchayati Raj Institutions have joined the AuditOnline system. Under the Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA) Scheme, 3.33 crore property cards have been generated for 2.06 lakh villages, with loans of about ₹1,713 crore sanctioned and recognition of women as property owners encouraged.
Employment and livelihoods (Department of Rural Development).
The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in force since 1 July 2026, guarantees 125 days of wage employment every financial year to eligible rural households, with attendance through Face Authentication and digital payments. More than 31.69 crore person days have been generated, over 2.81 crore workers from about 2.23 crore households have received employment, and works are under way in nearly 2.31 lakh Gram Panchayats. An interim allocation of ₹93,841 crore has been made to States and Union Territories for 2026-27, and the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan enables the Gram Sabha to decide works according to local needs.
Safe drinking water and sanitation (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation).
Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, rural tap water connections have grown from about 3.23 crore households (17 per cent) to more than 16 crore (over 80 per cent), and Jal Arpan, the handing over of completed water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and communities, was also highlighted. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), 12.22 crore household toilets have been built and over 5.25 lakh villages (89.6 per cent) have declared themselves Open Defecation Free Plus (Model). The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were discussed during the gram sabhas, as Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 culminates.
Water security (Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation).
Through Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain, more than 1.55 crore artificial recharge and storage structures have been constructed with community participation, and an impact study of the first phase estimated groundwater recharge of 2.43 billion cubic metres. Revised watershed development norms have raised funding to ₹22,000 per hectare in plain areas and ₹28,000 in hilly and difficult areas, and reduced the project period from seven to five years. The Gram Sabha activities under Catch the Rain focused on raising awareness about rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and community-led water conservation. Local communities, Panchayati Raj representatives and district officials participated actively in the programme, which featured technical guidance, screening of awareness videos, tree plantation and
Shramdaan
activities, along with the administration of the
Jal Shapath
. The
Catch the Rain (CTR) Anthem
was also played and displayed to reinforce the message of conserving every drop of rainwater and mobilising collective action towards sustainable water management.
Food security and consumer protection (Departments of Food and Public Distribution, and Consumer Affairs).
Under One Nation One Ration Card, about 3.27 crore portability transactions take place every month, and the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to up to 81.35 crore beneficiaries, extended up to 2028. The National Consumer Helpline, available in 17 languages, received 3,42,371 calls in August 2026 against 78,477 in August 2019, and has facilitated refunds of over ₹105 crore since April 2025. The e-Jagriti platform has disposed of more than 2.55 lakh of 2.81 lakh cases instituted and received the Silver Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026.
Digital land records (Department of Land Resources).
Under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme, 99.90 per cent of Records of Rights and 97.4 per cent of cadastral maps have been digitised. Citizens in 31 States and Union Territories can access land records online, and in 24 states/UTs can download digitally signed records, safeguarding owners against fraudulent mutations and facilitating access to credit.
Awareness on other key national initiatives
Several Ministries/Departments extended valuable support in ensuring awareness at the village level. The Ministry of Home Affairs facilitated awareness on the new criminal laws, namely the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam; the Ministry of Cooperation on the Digital Transformation and Strengthening of Cooperatives; the Ministry of Women and Child Development on Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat; and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, in pursuit of safe, healthy, child marriage free and drug free villages. These Special Gram Sabhas reaffirmed the Gram Sabha as the foundation of participatory democracy and local governance. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj looks forward to the preparation of people-centred Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28 under the People’s Plan Campaign, towards building Sashakt, Atmanirbhar and Viksit Panchayats in the larger endeavour of Viksit Bharat.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches 'Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0'  Across Personnel, Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Ministries, Expanding Swachhata into a Wider Movement of Efficiency and Resource Management
subtitle:
Swachhata Evolves from Cleanliness Drive into Sustained Culture of Good Governance, Resource Optimisation and Public Service: Dr. Jitendra Singh 

₹5,102.91 Crore Generated from E-Waste and Scrap Disposal; Over 1,049 Lakh Sq. Ft. Office Space Freed in Five Years, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh 

Campaign Taken Forward at DoPT-DARPG, CSIR Headquarters and Ministry of Earth Sciences; Over 100 Science Institutions Join the Drive

CSIR’s Waste-to-Wealth Technologies Take Waste Management Beyond Disposal to Resource Recovery, Innovation and Value Creation
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Swachhata has evolved from an appeal for cleanliness into a sustained culture of good governance, efficient utilisation of public resources, reduction of pendency and responsible management of waste, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, While launching the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 today.
Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for Swachhata from the Red Fort in 2014, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the initiative gradually transformed into a people’s movement and subsequently became an institutional practice across Government offices. He said the campaign has continuously acquired new dimensions, from toilets and cleanliness to disposal of old files, redundant furniture, e-files and electronic scrap, thereby linking Swachhata with administrative efficiency, optimum use of public space and productive management of resources.
Dr. Jitendra Singh began the day by participating in the launch activities of Special Campaign 6.0 at the venue designated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). He participated in Shramdaan, plantation under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, and the symbolic commencement of weeding out old records, besides honouring Safai Mitras by distributing safety kits and sweets.
Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG; Smt. Rachna Shah, Secretary, DoPT; and Dr. Surendrakumar Bagde, Director General, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), were among the senior officers present. DARPG is the nodal department for the Special Campaign.
The Minister thereafter proceeded to CSIR Headquarters, where he took forward Special Campaign 6.0 across the scientific and technological ecosystem. Dr. Jitendra Singh led a mass cleanliness drive, participated in the Swachhata Signature Campaign and plantation drive, and felicitated Safai Mitras. Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology (DST); and Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), along with senior officials from DST, DBT and CSIR, participated in the programme. The activities at CSIR included review and disposal of obsolete records and scrap, workplace improvement and effective management of office spaces, with emphasis on Jan Bhagidari.
Speaking during the launch activities, Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled how the Swachhata movement, after its initial focus on sanitation, gradually entered Government offices and addressed the large accumulation of files and records that were no longer required but continued to occupy valuable space. He recalled that the exercise subsequently evolved into a dedicated annual campaign from 2 October to 31 October, with each successive campaign adding new dimensions. From physical files and discarded furniture, the exercise has expanded to e-files and e-scrap, reflecting the changing nature of Government workplaces and the growing need for responsible management of electronic assets.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of the Special Campaigns has demonstrated that systematic disposal of redundant material can create both financial value for the public exchequer and usable space for Government offices. Over the last five years, ₹5,102.91 crore has been generated through disposal of e-waste and scrap, while more than 1,049.54 lakh square feet of office space has been cleared and put to productive use. More than 180.48 lakh files have also been closed or weeded out and 24.20 lakh cleanliness sites identified and cleaned across the country.
The Minister said the space released through the campaign can subsequently be put to productive use, including creation of green areas and restoration of spaces that had remained blocked or underutilised. He said the annual campaign serves as a renewed commitment to a practice that should continue throughout the year, while the repeated campaigns have helped make Swachhata part of the working culture of Government institutions.
The Minister subsequently visited the Ministry of Earth Sciences, where e-waste and obsolete equipment from Prithvi Bhavan and Mausam Bhavan were taken up for disposal under Special Campaign 6.0. Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, was present during the programme and briefed the Minister on the items identified for disposal.
The inventory comprises 705 items in all. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the exercise at the Ministry of Earth Sciences is part of a wider campaign across the scientific ecosystem, with similar activities being undertaken by institutions under Earth Sciences, CSIR and DST. He said more than 100 science institutions have commenced the campaign from 2 October, taking the message of Swachhata and responsible disposal of obsolete material across the country's scientific institutions.
The Minister also connected the campaign with the larger Waste-to-Wealth dimension of India's scientific ecosystem, where the objective goes beyond disposal of waste to developing technologies that can convert waste into useful products, materials, energy and new economic opportunities. The CSIR portfolio includes technologies for municipal solid-waste management, recycling of plastic waste, recovery of critical metals and rare earth elements from e-waste, recycling of lithium-ion batteries, biomethanation, conversion of agro-waste into biodegradable products, wastewater resource recovery and utilisation of industrial waste for value-added products. These technologies have been transferred to industry and other organisations for application and further development.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of Special Campaigns demonstrates how a cleanliness initiative can progressively become an instrument of administrative reform, resource optimisation and institutional efficiency. In the scientific ecosystem, this approach is being extended further through technologies that enable waste to move through a larger value chain, from identification and disposal to recovery, recycling, innovation and wealth creation.
The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 will run from 2 October to 31 October 2026, following the preparatory phase undertaken by Ministries and Departments during September. The campaign focuses on Swachhata, reduction of pendency, review and weeding of records, efficient utilisation of office space, scientific disposal of e-waste and redundant material, and improved record management across Government offices. The campaign is being implemented as a whole-of-government effort, with institutional goals across Ministries and Departments.

title: Robotics to Become an Accelerating Tool in Every Specialty of Medicine: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Robotics, AI and Nanoscience to Create Larger Ecosystem for Precision Health Delivery and Precision Medicine: Dr. Jitendra Singh 

From Robotic Surgery to Robotic Medicine, Technology Will Find Applications Across Medical Specialties, says Dr. Jitendra Singh 

Dr. Jitendra Singh: Tele-Robotics Can Take Specialist Expertise to the Patient Across Geographical Boundaries 

AI and Robotics Can Help India Address Its Unique and Diverse Healthcare Challenges, Says Union Minster Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 OCT 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who is also a noted Physician and diabetologist, today said robotics is set to become an accelerating tool in every specialty of medicine, covering diagnostics as well as treatment and therapy.
He said robotics, together with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and nanoscience, would create a larger ecosystem for precision health delivery and precision medicine, with emerging technologies enabling increasingly personalised healthcare based on an individual’s genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns.
Dr. Jitendra Singh was delivering inaugural address at the International Conference of the "Society of Robotic Surgery" here. He said robotics should not be viewed as a technology confined to surgery but as a tool that would increasingly become part of different branches of medicine. “It’s a tool. It will happen everywhere,” he said, adding that while the present conference is focused on robotic surgery, the future could see the emergence of robotic medicine, robotic endocrinology and robotic cardiology, just as AI is finding applications across different medical specialties.
The Minister said medicine is entering an exciting phase of frontier practices, with the 21st century witnessing the emergence of AI, biotechnology, nuclear medicine and other technology-driven solutions. He said the next phase would see greater application of genetically driven diagnostic solutions, alongside advances in quantum technologies, nanomedicine and robotics.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said precision medicine would increasingly require treatment approaches tailored to individual patients, even when they are diagnosed with the same disease. Genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns, he said, would increasingly shape medical decision-making, making technology-enabled and personalised healthcare an important part of the future of medicine.
Referring to the Genome India Programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said 10,000 individuals have already been sequenced and expressed the hope that India could eventually move towards gene sequencing for every newborn. He said undertaking such detailed genetic sequencing for a population of 1.4 billion would require the optimal use of AI and robotics.
The Minister also spoke about the potential of nanomedicine in addressing longstanding healthcare challenges. Referring to efforts towards developing oral insulin, he said advances at the nano level could help overcome limitations associated with conventional drug delivery and open new possibilities for therapeutic interventions.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s size, diversity and geographical spread make technologies such as AI, robotics and tele-robotics particularly relevant for healthcare delivery. Sharing his experience with robotic ultrasonography, he said he had performed an ultrasound on a person located 10,000 kilometres away in Antarctica, demonstrating the possibilities of remotely enabled medical technologies.
Describing the potential transformation in the traditional model of specialist healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said, “Instead of the patient being referred to the doctor, it will be the doctor being referred to the patient.” He said tele-robotics could enable specialist expertise to reach patients across geographical boundaries, allowing advanced medical capabilities to be delivered without the patient necessarily having to travel to the specialist.
The Minister also spoke about India’s evolving disease profile, where infectious diseases continue to coexist with metabolic and lifestyle-related disorders. He said diseases traditionally associated with later stages of life are increasingly being seen among younger people, creating a complex healthcare landscape that requires both advanced technological tools and a more integrated and holistic approach.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the scale and diversity of India’s healthcare requirements make the adoption of new technologies particularly important. AI and robotics can serve as powerful facilitatory tools for health delivery across the country, while also supporting the transition towards precision and personalised medicine.
Dr. Jitendra Singh congratulated the organisers of SRS India 2026 for bringing robotic surgery into the domain of institutional learning, academics and professional conference platforms. He said the adoption of emerging technologies such as robotics would be essential to keep pace with the rapidly evolving landscape of medical science.

title: Sarbananda Sonowal Hails SCI as Anchor of India's Maritime & Shipbuilding Ambitions
subtitle: Union Minister hails Shipping Corporation of India's growth from 19 vessels to a 5.26-million-DWT fleet, ties its expansion to Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
Posted On:
                02 OCT 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal
called on the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) to take a leading role in India's drive toward self-reliant, globally competitive shipbuilding and maritime capacity, as the company marked 65 years of operations at a ceremony at the International Cruise Terminal
, Mumbai today.
Sarbananda Sonowal, who attended as the chief guest at the event, congratulated SCI on completing six and a half decades of service to the nation and highlighted the company's role in safeguarding India's energy and trade security, pointing specifically to its performance during the recent Strait of Hormuz crisis. The Union Minister called on SCI to help advance the government's Viksit Bharat and Atmanirbhar Bharat goals, framing a stronger national fleet as central to India's ambition of becoming a top shipbuilding and ship-owning nation by 2047.
"SCI is one of the clearest examples of India building its own strength at sea," Sonowal said. "As India works to become a top shipbuilding nation under Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, SCI's fleet, its people and its partnerships will be central to that mission."
Founded in 1961 as a liner shipping company with 19 vessels, SCI has grown into a diversified maritime enterprise operating 58 vessels totalling 5.26 million deadweight tonnage (DWT). The company's operations now span crude and product tankers, bulk and container shipping, LPG and LNG carriers, offshore services, passenger and coastal transport, project cargo, ship management, and shipbuilding consultancy.
"Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is no longer content to simply own ships
,
we are determined to build them, right here at home. SCI's growth over these decades shows what Indian enterprise can achieve when backed by national resolve. As SCI expands its fleet and deepens its partnerships, it strengthens not just one company, but India's entire shipbuilding ambition, and carries us forward, mile by mile, toward the goal of a Viksit Bharat,"
Sarbananda Sonowal
said.
Nitesh Narayan Rane, Maharashtra's Minister for Fisheries and Ports
and Guest of Honour at the event, credited SCI's enduring ties to Maharashtra and Mumbai, and said a strong shipping ecosystem remained essential to trade, employment and the broader growth of India's maritime economy.
Capt. B.K. Tyagi, SCI's chairman and managing director,
outlined the company's plans for the years ahead, reaffirming its commitment to building a larger, modern and globally competitive fleet in support of the national push to expand India's shipping capacity and tonnage.
SCI is undertaking a fleet augmentation program backed by the government's expanded policy and financing support for the maritime sector, with proposed joint ventures involving Indian Oil's public sector undertakings and the Bharat Container Shipping Line laying the groundwork for accelerated expansion toward MAKV 2047 targets.
SCI is positioned to play a central role in strengthening India's maritime capacity, supporting the country's economic and energy security, and contributing to its broader shipbuilding and tonnage ambitions, as the company enters its next phase of growth toward a Viksit Bharat and Atmanirbhar Bharat.

title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar And Shri B. L. Verma Distribute 662 Aids, Assistive Devices Costing Over ₹10 Lakh Distributed To 114 Senior Citizens In Delhi-NCR Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
subtitle:
Government Reiterates Commitment To Ensuring Dignity, Independence And Quality Of Life For Senior Citizens

Dr Virendra Kumar Calls For Collective Efforts To Ensure Senior Citizens Live Their Life With Dignity, Respect And Honour

Shri B. L. Verma Lauds  Invaluable Contribution And Sacrifices Of Senior Citizens In The Nation-Building Process
date:

content:
The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised a distribution programme under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today.
During the programme,
662 aids and assistive devices, costing over
₹
10 lakh, were distributed to 114 senior citizens
residing in Senior Citizen Homes across Delhi-NCR.
The aids and assistive devices were distributed by
Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment
, and
Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment
.
Shri Sajeesh Kumar N., Joint Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
and

, were also present on the occasion.
